blocks.text: Rasulullaah ﷺ's Words to Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) when he Complained of His Sharp Tongue

Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) narrates that when he once complained to Rasulullaah ﷺ about his sharp tongue, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "How far you are from Istighfaar? I seek forgiveness from Allaah a hundred times daily." [^1] Another narration states that Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! My tongue is extremely sharp towards my family and I fear that it may enter me into Jahannam." The rest of the Hadith is as above. [^2]
Rasulullaah ﷺ's Statement about Seeking forgiveness Seventy times a Day

Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was on a journey when he said, 'Seek forgiveness from Allaah.' We then all engaged in Istighfaar. Rasulullaah ﷺ then instructed us saying, 'Complete this seventy times.' When we complied, Rasulullaah ﷺ said to us, 'When a male or female servant seeks forgiveness from Allaah seventy times a day, Allaah forgives seven hundred of his sins. Destroyed is that servant who commits more than seven hundred sins during any day and night.'" [^3]
The Incident of Hadhrat Ali (RA) with Rasulullaah ﷺ Concerning Istighfaar
Hadhrat Ali bin Rabee'ah narrates that Hadhrat Ali (RA) allowed him to ride behind him on his animal as he went to the outskirts of Harra. Hadhrat Ali (RA) then raised his head to the sky and said:

'O Allaah! Forgive my sins because none forgives sins but You'
Thereafter, he turned to me and laughed. 'O Ameerul Mu'mineen!' I asked, 'You have sought forgiveness from your Rabb and then turned to me to laugh?' He explained, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ allowed me to ride behind him on his animal as he went to the outskirts of Harra. Rasulullaah ﷺ then raised his head to the sky and said:
blocks.arabic_text: اَللّٰهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِيْ ذُنُوْبِيْ اِنَّهٗ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوْبَ اَحَدٌ غَيْرُكَ
